input.quote: 14.3 Choice of Law; Arbitration; Venue. This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of California, USA, excluding conflict of laws provisions and excluding the 1980 United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods. Any disputes arising out of this Agreement shall be resolved by binding arbitration in accordance with the then-current commercial arbitration rules of the American Arbitration Association ("RULES"). The arbitration shall be conducted by one (1) arbitrator appointed in accordance with the Rules in San Francisco County, California.
input.rationale: Governing law is California, which sits at our accepted fallback and needs no change. The forum, however, is mandatory single-arbitrator AAA arbitration in San Francisco rather than the corresponding California courts, so the fallback forum element fails on a material term. We therefore keep California law and substitute exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in San Francisco County, and conform the section heading and the Section 12.2 escrow cross-reference (which routed escrow disputes to arbitration under Section 14.3) so no dangling arbitration reference remains. We did not add a temporary-injunctive-relief carve-out, which is a preferred-level feature not required at the fallback.

proposal.summary: Replace mandatory AAA arbitration with exclusive jurisdiction of the California courts; California law unchanged.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] California law is acceptable to us, but our playbook requires disputes to go to courts rather than mandatory arbitration, so we have replaced the AAA arbitration mechanic with exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in San Francisco County, California, and conformed the heading and the escrow cross-reference.

ops.oldText: Any disputes arising out of this Agreement shall be resolved by binding arbitration in accordance with the then-current commercial arbitration rules of the American Arbitration Association ("RULES"). The arbitration shall be conducted by one (1) arbitrator appointed in accordance with the Rules in San Francisco County, California. A judgment upon the award may be entered in any court having jurisdiction of the parties, including without limitation the courts in San Francisco, California. The non-prevailing party in the arbitration shall pay all fees and charges of the American Arbitration Association; each party, however, shall be responsible for the payment of all fees and expenses connected with the presentation of its respective case.
ops.newText: Any disputes arising out of this Agreement shall be resolved exclusively in the state and federal courts located in San Francisco County, California, and each party submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of such courts.
